title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
summary: Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering. llm_summary: Australian researchers have succeeded in keeping a donated human liver functioning on a life‑support system for a record seven weeks, a milestone that could transform organ preservation and bio‑engineering. Led by surgeon‑inventor Carlo Pulitano, the team used a custom perfusion platform to supply the organ with nutrients, oxygen and waste removal, maintaining its viability far longer than traditional methods.
